title: Wave 6 Person-by-Person Global Royalty (Northern/Central Europe, Habsburgs, Windsors to 2026, Lombards, Iceland/Vinland, Wales, Rajputs, Ladakh, Moghulistan, Malay Annals, African Queens & Historical Figures)

nodes.name: King Eric VI the Victorious of Sweden (r. c. 970–995 CE)
nodes.notes: First historically verified king of unified Sweden; father of Olof Skötkonung.

nodes.name: King Olof Skötkonung of Sweden (r. 995–1022 CE; 1st Christian King)
nodes.notes: Father of Ingegerd of Sweden (+ Yaroslav the Wise) and Anund Jacob.

nodes.name: Princess Ingegerd Olofsdotter (St. Anna of Novgorod; Wife of Yaroslav the Wise)
nodes.role: Grand Princess of Kiev Linking Sweden to France, Hungary & England
nodes.notes: Married Yaroslav the Wise (1019 CE), mothering Anne of Kiev, Anastasia of Hungary, Elizabeth of Norway & Vsevolod I.

nodes.name: Birger Jarl of Bjälbo (Founder of Stockholm, r. 1248–1266 CE)
nodes.role: Bjälbo Regent & Father of Kings Valdemar & Magnus
nodes.notes: Married Ingeborg of Sweden (descendant of Munsö kings); consolidated medieval Sweden.

nodes.name: King Charles IX of Sweden (Son of Gustav I Vasa, r. 1604–1611)
nodes.notes: Father of Gustavus Adolphus.

nodes.name: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden (r. 1611–1632; Lion of the North)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Christina.

nodes.name: Queen Christina of Sweden (r. 1632–1654)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Gustavus Adolphus.

nodes.name: King Charles XII of Sweden (r. 1697–1718)
nodes.notes: Great Northern War commander.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden (b. 1946; Great-Grandson of Queen Victoria via Princess Margaret!)
nodes.notes: Descendant of both Gustav Vasa and Queen Victoria.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden (b. 1977; Future Queen)
nodes.role: Heir Apparent to the Swedish Throne
nodes.notes: Eldest child of King Carl XVI Gustaf.

nodes.name: King Gorm the Old of Denmark (r. c. 936–958 CE; Jelling Stones)
nodes.notes: Father of Harald Bluetooth.

nodes.name: King Harald I Bluetooth of Denmark & Norway (r. c. 958–986 CE; Christianizer)
nodes.notes: Father of Sweyn Forkbeard.

nodes.name: King Sweyn Forkbeard (+ Gunhild/Sigrid of Poland; King of Denmark & England, d. 1014)
nodes.role: Father of Cnut the Great & Estrid
nodes.notes: Fathered Cnut the Great.

nodes.name: King Valdemar I the Great of Denmark (r. 1157–1182; Grandson of Harald & Kiev!)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Estrid Svendsdatter & Yaroslav the Wise via Canute Lavard & Ingeborg of Kiev.

nodes.name: Queen Margaret I of Denmark, Norway & Sweden (Architect of Kalmar Union, 1397)
nodes.notes: Founder of the Kalmar Union.

nodes.name: King Christian IV of Denmark & Norway (r. 1588–1648; Oldenburg)
nodes.role: Brother of Queen Anne (+ James VI & I)
nodes.notes: Uncle of King Charles I of England.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Frederik X of Denmark (b. 1968; Glücksburg Heir of Christian IV & Victoria)
nodes.notes: Acceded in 2024.

nodes.name: Queen Emma of Normandy (Daughter of Richard I; Wife of Ethelred II & Cnut; Mother of Edward the Confessor & Harthacnut)
nodes.role: Twice Queen of England & Normandy Bridge
nodes.notes: Bridged Norman Dukes with Anglo-Saxon and Danish crowns.

nodes.name: Duke Mieszko I of Poland (r. c. 960–992 CE; Baptism of Poland 966)
nodes.notes: Father of Boleslaw I & Gunhild/Sigríðr.

nodes.name: King Boleslaw I the Brave of Poland (r. 992–1025; 1st Crowned King)
nodes.notes: Father of Mieszko II.

nodes.name: King Mieszko II Lambert of Poland (r. 1025–1034)
nodes.notes: Father of Casimir I.

nodes.name: Duke Casimir I the Restorer (+ Maria Dobroniega of Kiev, r. 1039–1058)
nodes.notes: Married Yaroslav the Wise's sister Maria Dobroniega of Kiev.

nodes.name: King Casimir III the Great of Poland (r. 1333–1370; Codifier & University Founder)
nodes.notes: Great lawgiver; sister Elizabeth married Charles I of Hungary -> Louis the Great.

nodes.name: Princess Gunhild / Świętosława of Poland (Daughter of Mieszko I; Mother of Cnut the Great)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Mieszko I who wed Eric the Victorious of Sweden and Sweyn Forkbeard of Denmark.

nodes.name: Princess Maria Dobroniega of Kiev (Daughter of St. Vladimir; Wife of Casimir I)
nodes.role: Sister of Yaroslav & Duchess of Poland
nodes.notes: Daughter of St. Vladimir the Great of Kiev; mother of Boleslaw II & Wladyslaw Herman.

nodes.name: King Mindaugas of Lithuania (r. c. 1236–1263)
nodes.notes: United Baltic Aukštaitija.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania (r. 1316–1341; Founder of Vilnius)
nodes.notes: Father of Algirdas and Kęstutis.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Algirdas (+ Uliana of Tver, r. 1345–1377)
nodes.notes: Wed Rurikid Princess Uliana of Tver.

nodes.name: King Wladyslaw II Jagiello (1386–1434; Victor of Grunwald 1410)
nodes.notes: Wed Queen Jadwiga of Poland, uniting Poland and Lithuania.

nodes.name: King Casimir IV Jagiellon (Son of Jagiello, r. 1447–1492)
nodes.notes: Father of Kings of Poland, Bohemia & Hungary.

nodes.name: King Sigismund I the Old (+ Bona Sforza, r. 1506–1548)
nodes.notes: Son of Casimir IV.

nodes.name: King John III Sobieski of Poland-Lithuania (r. 1674–1696; Relief of Vienna 1683)
nodes.notes: Maternal lineage connected back to Rurikid & Polish nobility.

nodes.name: Grand Duke Vytautas the Great of Lithuania (Son of Kęstutis; Cousin of Jagiello, 1392–1430)
nodes.notes: Daughter Sophia of Lithuania married Grand Prince Vasily I of Moscow.

nodes.name: Queen St. Jadwiga of Poland (Daughter of Louis I of Hungary; Rex Poloniae, 1384–1399)
nodes.notes: Married Grand Duke Jagiello (Wladyslaw II), uniting Poland & Lithuania.

nodes.name: Chieftain Álmos (Father of Árpád, c. 820–895 CE)
nodes.notes: Led Magyars westward.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Árpád of Hungary (r. c. 895–907 CE; Conquest of Carpathian Basin)
nodes.notes: Father of Zoltán.

nodes.name: King St. Stephen I of Hungary (r. 1000–1038 CE; 1st Christian King)
nodes.notes: Great-great-grandson of Árpád; wed Gisela of Bavaria.

nodes.name: King Andrew I of Hungary (+ Anastasia of Kiev, r. 1046–1060)
nodes.notes: Married Anastasia Yaroslavna of Kiev.

nodes.name: King Béla III of Hungary (+ Margaret of France, r. 1172–1196)
nodes.notes: Father of Andrew II.

nodes.name: King Andrew II of Hungary (r. 1205–1235; Golden Bull 1222)
nodes.role: Father of St. Elizabeth & Béla IV
nodes.notes: Issued the Golden Bull of 1222.

nodes.name: King Béla IV of Hungary (Rebuilder after Mongol Invasion, r. 1235–1270)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Charles I & Kunigunda of Bohemia.

nodes.name: King Louis I the Great of Hungary & Poland (Anjou-Capet, r. 1342–1382)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Jadwiga of Poland and Queen Mary of Hungary.

nodes.name: Princess St. Elizabeth of Hungary (Daughter of Andrew II, 1207–1231)
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Andrew II & Gertrude of Merania.

nodes.name: Regent John Hunyadi (Defender of Belgrade 1456, d. 1456)
nodes.notes: Father of King Matthias Corvinus.

nodes.name: King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary (r. 1458–1490; Bibliotheca Corviniana)
nodes.notes: Son of John Hunyadi; famed Renaissance patron.

nodes.name: Duke St. Wenceslas I of Bohemia (Přemyslid Martyr, r. 921–935 CE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of St. Ludmila & Bořivoj I.

nodes.name: King Ottokar II of Bohemia (r. 1253–1278; + Kunigunda of Kiev/Hungary)
nodes.role: Iron and Golden King of Bohemia
nodes.notes: Married Kunigunda (granddaughter of Béla IV & Rostislav of Kiev).

nodes.name: Emperor & King Charles IV of Bohemia (r. 1346–1378; Golden Bull & Charles Univ.)
nodes.notes: Son of Queen Elisabeth of Bohemia (Přemyslid); father of Sigismund & Anne of Bohemia.

nodes.name: Queen Anne of Bohemia (Daughter of Charles IV; Wife of King Richard II of England)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Emperor Charles IV who wed King Richard II.

nodes.name: Princess Bonne of Bohemia (Sister of Charles IV; Wife of King John II of France)
nodes.role: Ancestral Mother of Valois Kings of France
nodes.notes: Mother of Charles V the Wise of France.

nodes.name: Emperor Sigismund of Luxembourg (Son of Charles IV; King of Hungary & Bohemia)
nodes.notes: Daughter Elizabeth of Luxembourg wed Habsburg Albert II.

nodes.name: Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine (Duchess of Aquitaine; Queen of France & England, 1122–1204)
nodes.role: Mother of Richard I, King John & Eleanor of Castile
nodes.notes: Mother of Europe's greatest medieval royal network.

nodes.name: Queen Blanche of Castile (Granddaughter of Eleanor; Mother of King St. Louis IX of France)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Alfonso VIII & Eleanor of England; mother of St. Louis IX.

nodes.name: Queen Juana of Castile & Aragon ('Juana la Loca', Daughter of Ferdinand & Isabella, 1479–1555)
nodes.notes: Married Philip the Handsome; mother of Emperor Charles V & Ferdinand I.

nodes.name: Archduke Philip the Handsome of Burgundy (Son of Emperor Maximilian I; Father of Charles V)
nodes.role: Habsburg Prince & King Consort of Castile
nodes.notes: Son of Maximilian I & Mary of Burgundy.

nodes.name: Queen Catherine of Aragon (Daughter of Ferdinand & Isabella; Mother of Mary I of England)
nodes.role: Spanish Princess & 1st Queen of Henry VIII
nodes.notes: Mother of Queen Mary I.

nodes.name: Emperor Ferdinand I (Son of Philip & Juana; King of Bohemia & Hungary, 1556–1564)
nodes.notes: Brother of Charles V.

nodes.name: Emperor Joseph II (Eldest Son of Maria Theresa, r. 1765–1790)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Empress Maria Theresa.

nodes.name: Emperor Leopold II (Son of Maria Theresa; Father of Emperor Francis II, r. 1790–1792)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Habsburg Emperor Franz Joseph.

nodes.name: Queen Marie Antoinette of France (Daughter of Maria Theresa; Wife of Louis XVI, d. 1793)
nodes.role: Archduchess of Austria & Queen of France
nodes.notes: Daughter of Empress Maria Theresa.

nodes.name: Napoleon II Bonaparte ('L'Aiglon', King of Rome; Son of Napoleon I & Marie Louise, 1811–1832)
nodes.notes: United Bonaparte and Habsburg bloodlines.

nodes.name: Cosimo de' Medici ('Pater Patriae' of Florence, 1389–1464)
nodes.notes: Patron of Renaissance humanism.

nodes.name: Lorenzo de' Medici ('Il Magnifico', 1449–1492; Patron of Leonardo & Michelangelo)
nodes.role: Grandson of Cosimo; Father of Pope Leo X
nodes.notes: Great Renaissance statesman.

nodes.name: Queen Catherine de' Medici (Great-Granddaughter of Lorenzo; Queen of France by Henry II)
nodes.role: Mother of Francis II, Charles IX & Henry III
nodes.notes: Dominant Renaissance queen mother of Valois France.

nodes.name: Queen Marie de' Medici (Granddaughter of Emperor Ferdinand I; Wife of King Henry IV of France)
nodes.role: Mother of Louis XIII & Queen Henrietta Maria
nodes.notes: Mother of Louis XIII and grandmother of Charles II & James II of England.

nodes.name: German Emperor Kaiser Wilhelm I of Prussia (1797–1888)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Frederick William & Hohenzollern electors.

nodes.name: Empress Victoria / Princess Royal (Eldest Daughter of Queen Victoria; Mother of Kaiser Wilhelm II)
nodes.notes: Married Frederick III of Prussia.

nodes.name: German Emperor Frederick III (Son of Wilhelm I; Husband of Victoria, r. 1888)
nodes.role: German Emperor & Father of Wilhelm II
nodes.notes: Father of Kaiser Wilhelm II.

nodes.name: German Emperor Kaiser Wilhelm II (Son of Frederick III & Victoria, r. 1888–1918)
nodes.role: Last German Emperor & Grandson of Queen Victoria
nodes.notes: First cousin of King George V and Tsaritsa Alexandra.

nodes.name: Electress Sophia of Hanover (Granddaughter of King James I; Act of Settlement 1701)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Elizabeth Stuart & Frederick V; mother of King George I.

nodes.name: King Edward VII (Son of Queen Victoria & Prince Albert, r. 1901–1910)
nodes.notes: Married Alexandra of Denmark.

nodes.name: King George V (Son of Edward VII; Renamed House of Windsor 1917, r. 1910–1936)
nodes.notes: Father of Edward VIII & George VI.

nodes.name: King George VI (Son of George V, r. 1936–1952)
nodes.notes: Father of Queen Elizabeth II.

nodes.name: Queen Elizabeth II (r. 1952–2022; Longest-Reigning British Monarch)
nodes.role: Queen of the United Kingdom & Commonwealth
nodes.notes: Daughter of George VI; wed Prince Philip of Greece & Denmark.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Charles III of the United Kingdom (b. 1948, r. 2022–present)
nodes.role: Reigning Sovereign of the United Kingdom
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Queen Elizabeth II & Prince Philip.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): William, Prince of Wales (b. 1982; Son of King Charles III & Diana)
nodes.role: Heir Apparent to the British Crown
nodes.notes: Father of Prince George, Princess Charlotte & Prince Louis.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Prince George of Wales (b. 2013; Future Windsor Heir)
nodes.notes: 2nd in line to the British throne.

nodes.name: Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg & Gotha (1819–1861; Consort of Queen Victoria)
nodes.role: Father of Nine Royal Children Across Europe
nodes.notes: First cousin and husband of Queen Victoria.

nodes.name: Emperor Paul I of Russia (Son of Peter III & Catherine II, r. 1796–1801)
nodes.notes: Father of Emperors Alexander I & Nicholas I.

nodes.name: Emperor Alexander I of Russia (r. 1801–1825; Defeated Napoleon 1812)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Paul I.

nodes.name: Emperor Alexander II the Liberator (Son of Nicholas I, r. 1855–1881)
nodes.notes: Father of Alexander III; grandfather of Nicholas II.

nodes.name: Emperor Tsar Nicholas II (Son of Alexander III, r. 1894–1917)
nodes.notes: Married Alix of Hesse (Empress Alexandra, granddaughter of Queen Victoria).

nodes.name: Grand Duchess Anastasia Nikolaevna (Daughter of Nicholas II & Alexandra, 1901–1918)
nodes.role: Youngest Daughter of Tsar Nicholas II
nodes.notes: Great-granddaughter of Queen Victoria.

nodes.name: Empress Alexandra Feodorovna / Alix of Hesse (Granddaughter of Queen Victoria; Wife of Nicholas II)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Princess Alice (daughter of Queen Victoria).

nodes.name: Princess Anna Komnene (1083–1153; Historian Author of The Alexiad)
nodes.role: Daughter of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos
nodes.notes: Renowned medieval historian of the Komnenian Byzantine court.

nodes.name: Princess Zoe / Sophia Palaiologina (Niece of Constantine XI; Wife of Ivan III of Moscow)
nodes.role: Byzantine Heir Bridging Constantinople to Moscow
nodes.notes: Grandmother of Tsar Ivan IV the Terrible.

nodes.name: Matriarch Gambara of the Winnili / Lombards (Paul the Deacon Book I)
nodes.notes: Counselor mother of Ibor and Aio.

nodes.name: Duke Ibor & Duke Aio (Sons of Gambara)
nodes.notes: Led the Lombards out of Scandinavia.

nodes.name: King Agelmund (Son of Aio; 1st King of Lombards, 33 yrs)
nodes.notes: First crowned king in Historia Langobardorum.

nodes.name: King Alboin of Lombardy (Son of Audoin; Conqueror of Italy 568 CE)
nodes.role: Founder of Lombard Kingdom of Italy
nodes.notes: Conquered northern Italy (Lombardy).

nodes.name: King Authari (+ Catholic Queen Theodelinda of Bavaria, r. 584–590 CE)
nodes.notes: Married Bavarian princess Theodelinda.

nodes.name: King Rothari (Promulgated Edictum Rothari 643 CE)
nodes.notes: Codified Lombard customary law.

nodes.name: King Liutprand of the Lombards (r. 712–744 CE)
nodes.notes: Height of Lombard Italy.

nodes.name: King Desiderius of the Lombards (Last King, r. 756–774 CE; Father-in-Law of Charlemagne)
nodes.notes: Daughter Desiderata wed Charlemagne.

nodes.name: Queen Theodelinda of the Lombards (c. 570–628 CE; Correspondent of Pope Gregory I)
nodes.notes: Bridged Lombard royalty with Catholic Europe.

nodes.name: Ingólfur Arnarson (1st Permanent Settler of Iceland at Reykjavik, 874 CE)
nodes.notes: First Norse landnámsmaðr of Iceland.

nodes.name: Jarl Ketil Flatnose (Hebridean Norse Lord; Father of Aud the Deep-Minded)
nodes.notes: Father of Aud the Deep-Minded.

nodes.name: Aud / Unn the Deep-Minded (Matriarch Settler of Western Iceland)
nodes.role: Ancestress of Snorri Sturluson & Western Clans
nodes.notes: Widow of Olaf the White of Dublin who settled Breiðafjörður.

nodes.name: Erik the Red / Eiríkr Þorvaldsson (Founder of Norse Greenland, 985 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Leif Erikson.

nodes.name: Leif Erikson ('Leif the Lucky', Landed in Vinland / North America c. 1000 CE)
nodes.role: First Known European to Reach North America
nodes.notes: Son of Erik the Red who explored Helluland, Markland & Vinland (Newfoundland).

nodes.name: Gudrid Thorbjarnardóttir (Mother of Snorri Thorfinnsson, First European Born in America)
nodes.role: Matriarch Explorer of Vinland & Rome Pilgrim
nodes.notes: Married Thorstein (son of Erik the Red) & Thorfinn Karlsefni.

nodes.name: King Cunedda Wledig (Founder of Kingdom of Gwynedd, c. 400 CE)
nodes.notes: Migrated from Manaw Gododdin to North Wales.

nodes.name: King Maelgwn Gwynedd (Great-Grandson of Cunedda, d. 547 CE)
nodes.notes: Contemporary of Gildas.

nodes.name: King Cadwaladr ap Cadwallon ('Fendigaid', d. 682 CE; Red Dragon Ancestor)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the Welsh Red Dragon banner.

nodes.name: King Rhodri Mawr / Rhodri the Great (r. 844–878 CE)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of medieval Welsh royal lines.

nodes.name: King Hywel Dda ('Hywel the Good', Grandson of Rhodri Mawr; Lawgiver, d. 950)
nodes.notes: United nearly all Wales.

nodes.name: King Gruffydd ap Llywelyn (Sole Unifier of All Wales, r. 1055–1063)
nodes.notes: Contemporary of Edward the Confessor & Harold II.

nodes.name: King Owain Gwynedd (r. 1137–1170; Grandfather of Llywelyn the Great)
nodes.role: 1st Prince of Wales in Contemporary Charters
nodes.notes: Defeated Henry II's campaigns in Gwynedd.

nodes.name: Prince Llywelyn ap Iorwerth / Llywelyn the Great (r. 1195–1240; + Joan dau. of King John!)
nodes.role: Great Prince of Aberffraw & Lord of Snowdon
nodes.notes: Married Princess Joan (daughter of King John of England).

nodes.name: Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffydd ('The Last', Grandson of Llywelyn the Great, d. 1282)
nodes.role: Last Sovereign Prince of Independent Wales
nodes.notes: Fell in 1282 against Edward I.

nodes.name: Owen Tudor / Owain ap Maredudd (Kinsman of Llywelyn; + Queen Catherine of Valois)
nodes.role: Grandfather of King Henry VII Tudor
nodes.notes: United Welsh Gwynedd royal line with French Valois & English Crown.

nodes.name: Bappa Rawal / Kalbhoja (Founder of Mewar Sovereignty, 734 CE)
sources: James Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Tradition traces from Lava -> Guhaditya -> Bappa Rawal.

nodes.name: Rana Kumbha of Mewar (r. 1433–1468; Builder of Vijay Stambh & Kumbhalgarh)
sources: James Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Repelled Malwa and Gujarat sultanates.

nodes.name: Rana Sanga / Sangram Singh (r. 1508–1528; Adversary of Babur at Khanwa)
sources: James Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Maharana Pratap.

nodes.name: Maharana Pratap of Mewar (r. 1572–1597; Battle of Haldighati 1576)
sources: James Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vols. 1-2
nodes.notes: Grandson of Rana Sanga; resisted Mughal Akbar from Kumbhalgarh & Chavand.

nodes.name: Rao Jodha of Marwar (Founded Jodhpur & Mehrangarh Fort, 1459 CE)
nodes.notes: Solar Rathore founder of Jodhpur.

nodes.name: Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber/Jaipur (r. 1699–1743; Jantar Mantar Founder)
nodes.notes: Kachwaha Suryavamshi king descended from Kusha.

nodes.name: Samrat Prithviraj Chauhan III of Ajmer & Delhi (r. 1178–1192 CE)
nodes.notes: Celebrated in North Indian epic history.

nodes.name: Rawal Jaisal of Jaisalmer (Founded Jaisalmer Fort, 1156 CE)
nodes.notes: Bhati Rajput tracing lineage from Krishna's Yadavas.

nodes.name: King Lhachen Palgyigon (1st Independent King of Ladakh / Maryul, c. 930 CE)
nodes.notes: Established the Yarlung Tibetan dynasty of Ladakh.

nodes.name: King Lhachen Bhagan (Founder of Namgyal Dynasty of Ladakh, c. 1460 CE)
nodes.notes: Inaugurated the Namgyal line.

nodes.name: King Sengge Namgyal ('Lion King' of Ladakh, r. 1616–1642; Built Leh Palace)
nodes.notes: Built nine-story Leh Palace & Hemis Monastery.

nodes.name: Khan Tughlugh Timur of Moghulistan (r. 1347–1363; 1st Muslim Eastern Chagatayid)
nodes.notes: Chagatayid khan of Kashgaria & Semirechye.

nodes.name: Khan Yunus Khan of Moghulistan (Maternal Grandfather of Mughal Emperor Babur, d. 1487)
nodes.notes: Grandfather of Emperor Babur via daughter Qutlugh Nigar Khanum.

nodes.name: Sultan Said Khan of Yarkand (Founder of Yarkent Khanate, r. 1514–1533)
nodes.notes: Led expeditions across the Pamirs & Ladakh.

nodes.name: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat (1499–1551; Ruler of Kashmir & Author of Tarikh-i-Rashidi)
nodes.notes: First cousin of Emperor Babur; conquered Kashmir (1540–1551).

nodes.name: Guru Nanak Dev Ji (1469–1539; Founder of Sikhism, Bedi Khatri Tradition)
nodes.notes: Founder of Sikhism.

nodes.name: Guru Gobind Singh Ji (1666–1708; 10th Guru & Founder of Khalsa, Author of Bachittar Natak)
nodes.notes: Founded the Khalsa (1699) and composed Bachittar Natak linking Sodhi/Bedi houses to Kusha/Lava.

nodes.name: Sultan Mansur Shah of Malacca (r. 1459–1477; Golden Age of Malacca)
nodes.notes: Expanded Malacca across the Malay Peninsula & Sumatra.

nodes.name: Sultan Mahmud Shah of Malacca & Johor (r. 1488–1528)
nodes.role: Last Sultan of Malacca & Founder of Johor Line
nodes.notes: Reigned during 1511; sons founded Perak and Johor sultanates.

nodes.name: Queen Amina of Zazzau / Zaria (fl. 16th c. CE; Warrior Queen in Kano Chronicle)
nodes.notes: Expanded Zazzau's walled trade cities across northern Nigeria.

nodes.name: Empress Eleni of Ethiopia (d. 1522; Regent Who Initiated Portuguese Alliance)
nodes.notes: Reigned across Ba'eda Maryam, Eskender, Na'od & young Lebna Dengel.

nodes.name: Empress Mentewab of Gondar (1706–1773; Regent for Iyasu II & Iyoas)
nodes.role: Builder of Qusquam Complex in Gondar
nodes.notes: Dominant Solomonic empress regent of 18th-century Gondar.

nodes.name: Empress Taytu Betul (1851–1918; Wife of Emperor Menelik II & Strategist of Adwa)
nodes.notes: Co-architect of the Victory of Adwa (1896).

nodes.name: Empress Dowager Cixi of Qing China (1835–1908; Regent of Tongzhi & Guangxu)
nodes.role: De Facto Ruler of Late Qing China
nodes.notes: Consort of Xianfeng; dominant regent from 1861–1908.

nodes.name: Emperor Puyi / Xuantong (1906–1967; Last Emperor of Qing China)
nodes.notes: Abdicated in 1912 as 12th and final Aisin Gioro emperor.

nodes.name: Fujiwara no Kamatari (614–669 CE; Co-Architect of Taika Reforms & Founder of Fujiwara)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Nakatomi/Ame-no-Koyane.

nodes.name: Lady Murasaki Shikibu (c. 973–1014 CE; Heian Court Author of The Tale of Genji)
nodes.role: Fujiwara Author at Empress Shōshi's Court
nodes.notes: Descendant of Fujiwara no Yoshifusa.

nodes.name: Rabbi Moses ben Maimon / Maimonides / Rambam (1138–1204; Mishneh Torah)
nodes.role: Sephardic Nagid & Author of Guide for the Perplexed
nodes.notes: Rabbi Moses ben Maimon / Maimonides / Rambam (1138–1204; Mishneh Torah).

nodes.name: Rabbi Abraham ben Maimon (1186–1237; Son & Nagid Successor of Rambam)
nodes.notes: Rabbi Abraham ben Maimon (1186–1237; Son & Nagid Successor of Rambam).

nodes.name: Ibn Sina / Avicenna (980–1037 CE; Author of Canon of Medicine)
nodes.notes: Ibn Sina / Avicenna (980–1037 CE; Author of Canon of Medicine).

nodes.name: Ibn Rushd / Averroes (1126–1198 CE; Cordoba Philosopher & Jurist)
nodes.notes: Ibn Rushd / Averroes (1126–1198 CE; Cordoba Philosopher & Jurist).

nodes.name: Omar Khayyam (1048–1131 CE; Nishapur Astronomer, Mathematician & Poet)
nodes.notes: Omar Khayyam (1048–1131 CE; Nishapur Astronomer, Mathematician & Poet).

nodes.name: Mevlana Jalal al-Din Rumi (1207–1273 CE; Mystical Poet of Balkh & Konya)
nodes.role: Sufi Poet & Founder of Mevlevi Tradition
nodes.notes: Mevlana Jalal al-Din Rumi (1207–1273 CE; Mystical Poet of Balkh & Konya).

nodes.name: Sultan Walad (1226–1312 CE; Son of Rumi & Organizer of Mevlevi Order)
nodes.notes: Sultan Walad (1226–1312 CE; Son of Rumi & Organizer of Mevlevi Order).

nodes.name: Marco Polo (1254–1324 CE; Venetian Traveler at Kublai Khan's Court)
nodes.notes: Marco Polo (1254–1324 CE; Venetian Traveler at Kublai Khan's Court).

nodes.name: Vasco da Gama (c. 1460–1524 CE; Navigator to India Under Manuel I)
nodes.role: 1st Count of Vidigueira & Viceroy of India
nodes.notes: Vasco da Gama (c. 1460–1524 CE; Navigator to India Under Manuel I).
